transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Card Member Services. My name is Julian. May I have your full name, please?
Customer: Hi, yes, my name is Gideon Park.
Agent: Hello, Mr. Park. For verification purposes, could you please provide your billing zip code and the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Sure thing. Zip code is 98221, and the last four numbers are 4018.
Agent: Thank you. You're all verified. How can I assist you with your account today?
Customer: Well, I was sitting down earlier going through my monthly budget spreadsheets, and I noticed something strange from a couple months back that I completely missed.
Agent: Okay, I can certainly take a look at your account history. What merchant is this for, and what amount are you looking at?
Customer: The place is Harborlight Inn, and the amount is $512.80.
Agent: Thank you. And what date was that posted to your account?
Customer: The charge date says August 04, 2026. It showed up on my August 14, 2026 statement.
Agent: Got it. And what happened with that purchase?
Customer: I see two separate charges of $512.80 from Harborlight Inn.
Agent: I see. Did you make a reservation with them around that time?
Customer: Yes, I had a two-night hotel stay with them in August. Everything went smoothly there, but looking at my statement now, I was charged twice.
Agent: Understood. Have you contacted Harborlight Inn regarding the second charge?
Customer: No, I haven't reached out to them yet. I only just saw it today while going over my personal budget.
Agent: All right. So to make sure I have all the details recorded correctly, you had a two-night stay at Harborlight Inn on August 4th, 2026, and your statement from August 14th shows two identical charges of $512.80.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
